title: LodCensus line builder overflows its stack buffer once a level truncates (snprintf return used as an unclamped offset)
label: harness
label_evidence: src/diag, gated by Opt().lodCensus (BANISHED_LOD_CENSUS); no retail counterpart
reachability: Only with BANISHED_LOD_CENSUS=1, at the frame-120 dump of a mesh whose 8 LOD levels have large or absurd distances or long fields
proof: Replay of scene_watch.cpp:717-721 at docs/history/review_20261103/static/semgrep/replays/lodcensus_overflow.cpp, run in WSL with: clang++-19 -g -O0 -fsanitize=address lodcensus_overflow.cpp -o lod && ./lod. The input is 8 levels whose distance is about 1e30; the census itself flags distances above 1e6 at line 725. Output: ==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow ... WRITE of size 87 ... #0 vsnprintf #1 snprintf #2 main lodcensus_overflow.cpp:10 ... 'buf' (line 8) <== Memory access at offset 680 overflows this variable.
root_cause: The loop does off += snprintf(buf + off, sizeof(buf) - off, ...) with no room test. After one call truncates, off is greater than 512, so sizeof(buf) - off (a size_t) wraps to about 2^64 and the next call writes past buf. The vb2[320] loop at line 735 has the same shape.
minimal_fix: Stop each loop when off >= (int)sizeof(buf) (or clamp off to sizeof(buf) - 1), as redzone_alloc.cpp:144 and stress_harness.cpp:1217 already do; same for the vo / vb2 loop at line 735.

title: Negative serialized array count: SetSizeCore destroys -n elements at old + n*stride (wild pointer free/release)
label: retail
label_evidence: array.cpp banner: SetSizeCore is retail 0x1800298f0. Its comment says 0x180026b50 (the destroy step) is called from both branches, including `old + newSize*stride`. Every caller is retail's `SerializeInt(n); if reading SetSize(n)`, and the comments carry the retail addresses: package_file_serialize.cpp 1800b617e, vtbatch7 SoundEffect::Serialize, animationstate.cpp 0x18005aa30/0x18005b1e0/0x18005c8a0.
reachability: Any .rsc in a mod .pkm: PackageFile (package metadata), SoundEffect, GraphicsMesh nodes, AnimationGroup keys. Also the AnimationManager save state in a shared .sav.
proof: Inputs in scratchpad/crashes/rsc_serialize/: pkg-negcount-setsize (45 B), soundeffect-negcount-setsize (25 B, hex 03aaaaaaaa00000000000000000000803f00000000ffffffff), meshnodes-negcount-setsize (17 B, hex 05aaaaaaaa0000000000000000ffffffff). Repro: wsl ~/fz/rsc_serialize/fuzz_rsc_serialize <file>. Masked build: 'AddressSanitizer: SEGV ... #0 rtcoll::ReleaseStringsCounted array_destroy.cpp:451 #1 IO::PackageFile::Serialize package_file_serialize.cpp:215'; 'SEGV #0 rtcoll::FreeInnerArraysCounted array_destroy.cpp:439 #1 Audio::SoundEffect::Serialize vtbatch7_soundbuffer_soundeffect.cpp:630'. Unmasked build: 'array.cpp:2312:36: runtime error: applying non-zero offset 18446744073709551608 to null pointer #0 rtcoll::SetSizeCore #1 IO::PackageFile::Serialize :215'. The fuzzer also reached the same site through RtGraphics_SerializeAnimInstances animationstate.cpp:353/358 (FreeInnerArraysCore).
root_cause: The count is read straight from the stream and passed to SetSize(int) with no sign check. With newSize < 0 == oldSize - k: the grow branch is skipped, the element loop is empty, and the shrink arm runs `spec->destroy(nullptr, old + newSize*stride, oldSizeI - newSize)`. That releases Strings or frees inner arrays at an address below the buffer (below null on a fresh object), and _size is left negative. On a non-empty array this frees heap memory the array does not own.
minimal_fix: In SetSizeCore, reject newSize < 0 (treat it as 0, or fail the read) before any pointer arithmetic, with a comment that retail has the same arm. Alternatively, validate the count at each Serialize read site (count < 0 -> stop reading).

label: ext

proof: Replay at docs/history/review_20261103/static/semgrep/replays/async_create_exit.cpp: namespace-scope mutex, condition_variable and deque; two detached workers parked in g_workCv.wait; then main returns. Size probe (scratchpad/xwma/size_probe.cpp, built against the same archive): ~/fz/xwma/size_probe scratchpad/crashes/xwma/huge_total.bin
